quest.title: What the Blue Flowers Left Behind
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

chapter.num: True Tales of the Violet Garden: Act II
chapter.title: What the Blue Flowers Left Behind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there! You must be visiting from Liyue to participate in the Irodori Festival. We'll be your guides and will take you onto the island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, is it Paimon or have we met somewhere before?

dialogues.speaker: Xu
dialogues.text: Haha. Yes, in fact, we have. I am Xu from Feiyun Commerce Guild. Aboard this ship, we have calligraphers, painters, and even players of Theater Mechanicus.

dialogues.speaker: Xu
dialogues.text: The inventor of Theater Mechanicus previously came to the Feiyun Commerce Guild seeking investment. Although the guild manager was not interested, Master still wanted to support them.

dialogues.speaker: Xu
dialogues.text: We heard that they'd be demonstrating the game and letting people try Theater Mechanicus at the Irodori Festival. So the guild manager instructed Master and I to take the opportunity to come to Inazuma and investigate the product's potential.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, speaking of which, where's the young master?

dialogues.speaker: Xu
dialogues.text: Ah, well... Master, he's uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Xingqiu's just sitting there... sound asleep!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: ...Huh, wha—

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: #Oh... *yawn* It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I presume you are guests in Inazuma as well? It seems fate has destined our paths to cross once again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We aren't actually guests, we're actually guides for the Irodori Festival.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Please, no need to worry. I was a little too caught up in a novel on the voyage here. When I finally realized what time it was, the first rays of dawn were already peeking over the horizon.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Ah yes, now that we've arrived, the Kanjou Commission will likely wish to inspect our invitation letter. Let's keep it in hand, shall we?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Huh, that's odd...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: There was a piece of paper underneath my bag... Strange, I don't recall seeing it there before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon have a look!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* There's no doubt about it! It's from the same series as the story we found before. Even the handwriting looks exactly the same!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: The story you found before?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, in the warehouse down by the—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ahem!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, by the... the Poem Hunt competition!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's it! A friend of ours is on Ritou to paint portraits of The Five Kasen... You know, as part of the Irodori Festival. Poetic stories about The Five Kasen have been hidden in various places nearby!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you can find one of the stories and give it to this friend of ours, then there's a chance you'll become the model for the next portrait!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Wait a moment, so you mean that...

choices.text: Uh oh, he's on to us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey, it's hard coming up with stuff on the spot like that!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: ...There is a chance of meeting Calx in person!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, uh, yeah... you could say that.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Really? That's wonderful! I knew that Calx would attend the Irodori Festival, but convincing my father to let me come to Inazuma was proving to be quite the high hurdle. I had to really rack my mind to come up with the excuse of evaluating the investment value of Theater Mechanicus.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Just a few days later, word then came that Calx would be busy painting portraits of The Five Kasen during the festival.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: It is a most rare opportunity for both Calx and I to be in Inazuma together, but it seemed he would be too busy with the portraits to meet with me... So, I've felt quite disappointed for some time now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, Xingqiu. Even though Calx has work to do, he still has time to see friends. We can take you to see him right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, we heard that Calx did illustrations for your A Legend of Sword novel.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Ah, so you've already heard.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: To be honest, my works have drawn little interest in Liyue. However, the novels are selling quite well in Inazuma with the help of Calx's beautiful illustrations.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Calx is not only a skilled artist, but he also carries out his craft with great alacrity. I heard that it took him merely a few hours to finish the illustrations for the latest chapter.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: But when I looked at the art, the brushwork did not even look the slightest bit rushed. His work is truly exquisite...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh my, I was beginning to get carried away there. Let us depart, quickly now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew... Luckily, the idea of meeting Albedo managed to draw Xingqiu's attention and keep the situation under wraps. Let's just hope we don't let anything slip while meeting Albedo.

choices.text: Paimon, you're so terrible at making up stories!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon, how are you? And who is this accompanying you?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You must be Calx, it's a great pleasure to finally meet you. I am the author of A Legend of Sword, Zhen...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Ah, forgive me... It's rude of me to introduce myself by my pen name when meeting in person. Please, call me Xingqiu.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And you may call me Albedo, then.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: No, no, that would be most improper...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Why not? Seeing as we are both friends of {NICKNAME}, it'd be more convenient for us to use our real names.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Besides, we've already corresponded with each other many times before. In fact, I feel a bit self-conscious seeing you act so politely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's not just you, Albedo. We haven't seen Xingqiu act this awkward before either.

choices.text: It's a real eye-opener, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Ahem... you guys... It's certainly not good taste for you two to be teasing me like that.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh, by the way, we happened to find a story from the Poem Hunt competition at the docks. I heard that you are collecting them.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Hmm? Poem Hunt?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You know... The thing where we have to find pieces of paper with stories of The Five Kasen! Uh, Venti found one and then he was allowed to be a model for one of your portraits, hehe.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Huh?... Oh, yes. That's right.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You show Albedo the piece of paper found by Xingqiu...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I understand the story now. Thank you, it's very helpful.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Splendid. Though, I'm still piecing together the story myself. Would you kindly explain it to me in more detail?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If all of you are free, why don't we discuss this over a meal?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Ah, well, about that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you have other plans, Xingqiu?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: No no, not at all! Speaking of dining, Shimura's Unagi Chazuke is quite delicious, would you like to go there?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Shimura's? Unfortunately, today is a bit windy, how about Uyuu Restaurant instead?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: That's perfectly fine with me. But, I must first unpack my luggage. Let's meet later at Uyuu Restaurant.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Hmm, something didn't quite add up just now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, no way! Paimon thinks we acted well together. Did we say something we weren't supposed to?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #No, Paimon, I'm not referring to us. {NICKNAME}, what are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Xingqiu was a little suspicious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Xingqiu's suspicious? Hey, what are you two talking about?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Paimon, you read the poem, right? Although it may seem confusing to Xingqiu on its own, what if we read it together with the previous poem we found?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Read them together? Hmm, let's see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Suikou lost Aoi no Okina's poem in a drunken stupor, so Aoi no Okina recovered the poem and gave it to some mysterious person...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait a minute... Could today's story be hinting that the one who stole the latest copies of A Legend of Sword... Is Xingqiu himself!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way, that can't be right! Xingqiu only arrived at Inazuma this morning.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: And that is precisely the point of suspicion. If Xingqiu had only just arrived in Inazuma, how could he recommend Shimura's Chazuke?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Moreover, he didn't raise any questions when I suggested another place because of the windy weather. This means he knows that Shimura's is an open-air restaurant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Are you saying that Xingqiu has already been in Inazuma for some time and that he's only pretending he just arrived?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Yes, that is indeed my conclusion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, how could Xingqiu be the book thief!? His mission is to fight for justice, isn't it? There's no way he'd do something against his own ideals!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Calm down, Paimon. Even though this is the first time I've met Xingqiu in person, we've communicated via letters for some time now. I do have some understanding of his character.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I think there must be some deeper motive at play here. The story also tells us that Aoi no Okina flees with the poem because of a threat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Could Xingqiu be in danger?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: It's difficult to say at this point. But given that Uyuu Restaurant is indoors, it will be easy for us to detect anyone following or eavesdropping on us. I think it should be safe for us to talk there.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I'll be relying on your assistance to get to the bottom of this matter.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Good. Then let's head to Uyuu Restaurant.

choices.text: I learned some new tips on manners today.

talks.objective: Meet Albedo at The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Youta
dialogues.text: The last phase of the Irodori Festival is when they release all the new publications. The one I'm really looking forward to is A Legend of Sword!

dialogues.speaker: Akito
dialogues.text: That's right! A signed first edition is gonna become quite the collectible. I've gotta get my hands on a copy!

dialogues.speaker: Youta
dialogues.text: I've seen Zhenyu's signature before. His handwriting is super neat, he must be really diligent about his style.

dialogues.speaker: Akito
dialogues.text: He'll be there in person on the day of the release, so we'll get a good look at him then. I hear that he's actually pretty young.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, did you just hear that? Not only will Xingqiu be signing novels at the release... but his handwriting is "super neat"!?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I don't see anyone suspicious around, it seems clear for the moment. Let's go inside and wait for Xingqiu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, this whole thing's starting to make Paimon a little nervous. What do we do? And what do we talk about when Xingqiu gets here...?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: First, we must ascertain whether Xingqiu was already in Inazuma or not. If we can find evidence of him deceiving us, then we can use it as leverage to persuade him to tell us the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Since we're still waiting for him, why don't you go and chat with other guests in the restaurant and see if you can learn anything useful?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Hello there, what can I get for you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi, do you have any special recommendations today?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Why of course, I'd personally recommend our freshly caught seafood! It's been pouring these past few days, so the fishing boats haven't been able to sail at all. But the weather finally cleared up today, so we have some fresh catch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the weather at sea has been bad these past few days...

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: It sure has, a few guests from Liyue were just telling me that their boat was heaving and rolling all the way here. They couldn't do anything but sleep the entire trip.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, this might be some useful information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo, what should we talk about when Xingqiu gets here? Any ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm, I will try to break the ice by talking about our work on novels and illustrations.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If he really is hiding something, then he might feel even more nervous than we do. If we start by talking about our work creating novels, perhaps he will lower his guard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come to think of it, Xingqiu mentioned that he'd like to thank you for finishing the illustrations on time. He said they looked amazing despite the time you had.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Is that so? Hmm, that is also a very valuable clue.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Talk about the scenery on the journey.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: To be honest, there wasn't much to see, just water all around, morning to night. The sheer monotony of the trip caused everyone to grow a little impatient.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: So, when the peak of Mt. Yougou finally appeared in the distance as we approached the islands of Inazuma, everyone crowded the deck to have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: However, the ship sailed along at a crawling pace, it took a whole day from the time we saw the mountain peak to the time we docked.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't catch anything suspicious so far...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, there was something really suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... If it took an entire day to reach the docks, then it would have been pouring rain at the time they saw the top of the mountain!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We learned a couple of things from his account, but we still require more evidence. Let's discuss creating novels with Xingqiu.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: While it is entertaining to read novels, writing one is an endeavor of its own.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: You must give great thought to every detail, from the layout of the plot to the rhythm of the lines.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: And even when you have come up with interesting content, there's still no guarantee that it will be to your liking.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I couldn't agree more.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Whether it's writing a book, creating art, or studying alchemy, seldom can you really feel joy after seriously delving into the work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xingqiu and Albedo are getting into some deep topics now, but nothing suspicious has come up...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Talk about Albedo's illustrations.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Speaking of illustrations, Albedo, I've long wished to express my sincerest gratitude for providing the illustrations in my novel.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: My novel didn't sell well in Liyue, so I must admit that I had some reservations regarding its potential.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Yet you've consistently managed to select the most important scene of the chapter for your illustrations. This made me feel as though what I was trying to express could be understood, after all.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Thank you. However, I took some risks in the illustrations, so I'm feeling slightly uneasy myself.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Risks?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Light novel illustrations are typically centered around the characters, but this time, I adopted a different approach in the illustration for the last chapter.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Well, that scene was intended to depict the change in the world, so I thought it very fitting to draw only scenery.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, doesn't sound like anything suspicious has come up so far...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: No, there was a crack in his alibi. My illustrations were sent for printing the moment they arrived in Inazuma. So logically speaking, there's no way he could possibly know what the illustrations look like.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Xingqiu, we have something very important to ask you now.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh? Why the solemn looks all of a sudden...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Xingqiu, what's with the facade?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Huh? I'm afraid I don't follow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mr. Okazaki told us earlier that actually the weather at sea was very bad these last few days. So, when you said that everyone came running to the deck to see Mt. Yougou, that couldn't have happened.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: On top of that, the latest installment of A Legend of Sword will only be revealed at the Irodori Festival. Even we, the creators, haven't received a sample copy. If that's the case, how could you know what my illustrations look like?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Uh, well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The jig's up, Xingqiu. You were already in Inazuma before today, weren't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Are you in some kind of danger but can't tell us the truth? Don't worry, {NICKNAME} and Albedo are no pushovers, we can help you!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: No, no! Please, you misunderstand me.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: *sigh* I suppose my lack of sleep is inevitably taking its toll on my mind. I didn't notice for a moment that you were testing me at all.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I did in fact come to Inazuma early to handle some things. Let me consider how to explain this. *sigh* Oh, this is most embarrassing...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Oh ho? Well, if this isn't a coincidence! I didn't expect to see everyone here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Tone-Deaf Bard, what are you doing here...?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, I heard that the owner of this establishment has some fine aged wines. I didn't want to miss the opportunity to taste them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, Paimon knew you couldn't possibly be up to anything good.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Says who? In fact, I come as the bearer of good tidings.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I just bumped into Kujou Sara a moment ago. She said that the Tenryou Commission has apprehended the criminal who stole all those copies of A Legend of Sword. You needn't worry about it any longer.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Huh! The criminal who stole... A Legend of Sword!?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Uh, did I say something I shouldn't have?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh no! The person they apprehended... was it by chance an editor named Onodera?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Apologies, Kujou Sara didn't mention a name, but I saw her taking someone toward Hanamizaka.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Everyone, it's too late to explain. We must make haste and rescue Onodera!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Xingqiu arrives shortly after, and everyone enjoys a leisurely meal. Afterward...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: That was delicious. Inazuman cuisine largely consists of fresh seafood, which is certainly to my liking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's good, we were worried you might not have an appetite because you didn't sleep well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Now's our chance, {NICKNAME}. Let's talk to Xingqiu and see if he says anything useful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we could start by asking him about the journey.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Please wait, Onodera is innocent!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Oh, so you must be the author of A Legend of Sword. I didn't expect to see others tagging along with you.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Anyway, you mustn't take him away, I can explain everything...

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: No need to worry, Zhenyu! I've just explained everything to Madam Kujou, and Kuroda has testified for me.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Yes, in fact, we were just getting ready to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh, whew... what a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hmm, wait a minute! Does everyone else here already know?

dialogues.speaker: Tenryou Commission Soldier
dialogues.text: Heh...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Ahem! Well, to be precise, we had dispatched two additional squads here... In order to prevent the suspect from escaping.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xingqiu looks pretty flustered. What exactly is going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I bet it has something to do with his signature.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Ah, ahem... Though it's most embarrassing, it appears quite a few people are aware of the situation now. There's no use keeping it a secret...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: In the end, I'm the one responsible for this whole predicament.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: No, Zhenyu, it's only appropriate that I take responsibility for this. Everyone, please let me explain.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: For the Irodori Festival, I recommended the idea of selling newly released novels signed by the authors.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Not only was this the first major project that I was in charge of since joining the Yae Publishing House, but Lady Yae also gave me a lot of support.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: However, I did not discuss our plans with the authors in advance. As a result, it caused a great deal of trouble for Zhenyu.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Yes, to be frank, calligraphy is not my strong point, so signing events are really not my forte.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Even though such an event would be difficult for Zhenyu, after telling him how important the plans were to me, he immediately boarded a ship to Inazuma to come up with a solution.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: So these past few days, Zhenyu has been actively practicing his handwriting. However, it takes time to sign each book, and we realized the time we reserved for the signing was not nearly enough.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: So I came up with the idea of moving the new books from the warehouse to my place. That way, Zhenyu could use these few days to sign them all.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: I thought everything would work out without a hitch... I never expected that someone would immediately realize that the books were missing from the warehouse.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: To make things worse, I was on vacation and staying with Zhenyu in my house these past few days... I had no idea that the situation had turned into such a huge mess.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: *sigh* All of this happened because I wanted to prove myself through this event.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Onodera, I agreed to your proposal because I didn't want the readers to know of my unsightly handwriting.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Also, I knew that Onodera had been misled by one of my prior signatures.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: At a previous event, the Yae Publishing House had requested autographs of authors so they could be put on display.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I practiced tirelessly for an entire day to finally deliver a stylish and elegant signature for the event.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: But looking back on it now, I had dug myself into a hole by delivering that nice signature for the sake of my pride.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hey, c'mon you two, loosen up a little. The theft was nothing more than a simple misunderstanding. Besides, everyone has something they do not wish others to see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. All that matters is that Xingqiu and his books are okay.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Onodera, I think you should explain the truth regarding the stolen books to the rest of the people on Ritou.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Yes, I understand. I'll apologize to everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should probably be heading back to Ritou as well. Let's tag along.

talks.objective: Go to the Outlander Affairs Agency

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Onodera? What are you doing here? Aren't you supposed to be on leave these few days?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Onodera explains the situation to the editors.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: I'm very sorry for all the trouble that I've caused!

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes, Onodera, but...

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Why didn't you tell everyone earlier? If you had told us, we could've thought of some ways to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: That's right. We're a team, and we should be helping each other in tough situations like this.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Let's leave the past behind us now. Our first priority is to help Zhenyu with his signatures. How is your progress so far?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: My progress is not what I had hoped for... Even after working through the night these past few days, I've only finished perhaps one-tenth of the signatures.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no wonder Xingqiu looked so sleepy today.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: I understand. Murata, go back to Yae Publishing House and get Aratani to book a room on the second floor of the Uyuu Restaurant. We'll be using it for Zhenyu's emergency calligraphy lessons!

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Yes, Mr. Hirayama! It just so happens that my brother is a calligrapher, should I ask him to lend his assistance as well?

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Yes, good idea. Ah, you've just reminded me... Two calligraphers from Liyue arrived today. We have worked with them before, so I'll go and ask them to help out, too.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It seems I'm really in for it now...

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: No need to worry, Zhenyu. I'm sure you can do it! Didn't you finish the last chapter of your novel in just one week's time?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Yes, but writing novels and learning calligraphy are two entirely different skills!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though Xingqiu still has to deal with his handwriting issue, Paimon somehow feels a little relieved now.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I always used to prefer working alone in my workshop, but I have come to realize that solving problems with others also has its merits.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: We also owe a special ode of gratitude to the mysterious person who has been leaving important info for us along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean whoever left behind those stories about The Five Kasen?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Pardon me, but what are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh right, we haven't had a chance to explain things to Xingqiu yet.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain all that has happened in the past few days...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I see, it appears that Onodera and I were spotted when we were moving the books.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Albedo, may I ask you one thing? Are you able to include me in a portrait as well?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Not only do I owe the successful resolution of today's incident to that story, but I also hope that I'll remember this lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No problem. Considering the similarities between the portrait and the events that have taken place, your proposal is very reasonable.

talks.objective: Go to The Five Kasen Plaza
Talk to Paimon at The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo really is something. He finished the portrait of Aoi no Okina in no time at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wonder how Xingqiu's calligraphy training is going at Uyuu Restaurant. Hey, {NICKNAME}, do you think whoever left those stories for us could be hiding somewhere nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hellooo! Mr. story writer! Are you here? Uh, could you please help Xingqiu with something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's a friend of ours, and the release of his new book is super important to him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! What's that sound!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, it was just a cat. Looks like we can't make them reveal themselves that easily.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's getting late now. Let's go back and get some rest. We still have to go to the docks and wait for another ship tomorrow morning.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Talk about his thoughts regarding the journey.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well, I've never embarked on such a long journey before. Though I was quite excited when we set off, the long days at sea quickly became most monotonous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, speaking of the journey, did anything noteworthy happen along the way?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well, to be honest, I spent most of the trip with my nose in a novel, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that didn't tell us much...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Talk about the book he read during the voyage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, Xingqiu, what book were you reading on the way here?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh, I was reading a novel called, "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?". It was sent to me by my editor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't you feel dizzy while reading on the ship?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Haha, it was nothing I couldn't handle. Don't forget, I'm proficient in the arts of the Guhua Clan. That being said, there were quite a few people aboard who felt seasick.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, there doesn't seem to be anything suspicious about what he's said so far...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The passenger ship from Liyue that we're supposed to meet should be arriving soon. Let's go to the docks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know that Xingqiu will be on board, right? So we should be careful not to say anything about the stolen novels.
